items.q: It’s reported that a terrorist attack on a police facility in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on September 18 caused heavy casualties. Does China have a comment?
items.a: China strongly condemns this attack. We mourn for the loss of lives and extend sincere sympathies to the injured and the bereaved families. Terrorism is a common enemy of humanity. Fighting terrorism is in the shared interests of all countries. China will continue its steadfast support for Pakistan’s counter-terrorism efforts. We call on all countries to join forces in tackling the threat of terrorism and safeguard global security and stability.

items.q: On the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) put forward by President Xi Jinping, could you update us on the implementation of the initiative over the past five years? Is China considering hosting events on the initiative on the sidelines of the 81st sessio
items.a: Five years ago today, President Xi Jinping put forward the GDI at the general debate of the 76th session of the UN General Assembly. Focusing on development, a timeless theme for humanity, the initiative pools together international efforts to put development high on the global macro policy agenda, aims to expedite the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and has injected strong impetus into revitalizing global development. The initiative has received extensive recognition from the international community.

items.q: China just announced President Xi’s state visit to the United States. Could you please share more information about the schedule and China’s expectation for China-U.S. relations?
items.a: At the invitation of President Donald J. Trump, President Xi Jinping will soon pay a state visit to the United States. During his visit, President Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views with President Trump on major issues concerning bilateral ties and world peace and development. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to China-U.S. relations. items.q: A U.S. official said last week at a briefing that China has not fully resumed rare earth deliveries despite agreeing to do so at previous summits of the two leaders. What is China’s position?
items.a: I’d refer you to competent authorities for the specific question. China is committed to keeping the global industrial and supply chains of critical minerals safe and stable. China and the United States should jointly implement the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade ties.

items.q: The New Zealand Defence Force said today that two of its naval ships have transited the Taiwan Strait. The New Zealand PM called this a routine activity and said he was not expecting any backlash from China. Does China have any comment on this event?
items.a: China’s position on foreign military vessels’ transit through the Taiwan Strait is consistent.

items.q: New Zealand’s cyber security agency said China was the country’s most persistent and capable state-backed cyber threat. What is the ministry’s comment of this?
items.a: China opposes and resolutely fights hacker attacks in accordance with law, and opposes the dissemination of cyber security disinformation for political purposes. China urges the relevant agency in New Zealand to stop spreading lies and stoking discord, and instead do more to foster mutual understanding and trust between the two countries.

items.q: It has been almost a month since Gyirong County was hit by the devastating mudslide. Could you provide the latest casualty figures for foreign nationals and an update on the rescue operations?
items.a: The disaster left 261 foreign nationals unaccounted for. China has shared information with their countries’ embassies in Beijing.

items.a: The Chinese side has released a readout on the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues, which you may refer to. For further information, I’d refer you to competent authorities.

items.a: Protraction of the U.S.-Iran conflict does not serve the common interests of the parties concerned or the international community. It is vital for parties to choose peace, resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and restore peace and tranquility to the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date.

items.a: I’d refer you to competent authorities for any specifics regarding the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues.

items.a: The election of UN Secretary-General bears on the reform and development of the UN and the vital interests of member states. China supports the selection in accordance with the UN Charter of a new Secretary-General who observes the UN Charter, shows outstanding competence, is impartial and upright, and fulfills responsibilities with dedication. China will work with all relevant parties to participate in the election process in a responsible manner.

items.a: During the visit, the two presidents exchanged views on major international and regional issues of mutual interest. China’s position and policy on the Korean Peninsula issue maintains consistency and continuity.

items.a: Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao are part of China’s Nansha Qundao and Chinese territory. China has indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and its adjacent waters. The scope of Philippine territory is defined by several international treaties. China’s Nanhai Zhudao, including Nansha Qundao, lie beyond that scope. items.a: As this year’s host of APEC, China stands ready to work with all parties for fruitful outcomes of the APEC “China Year,” and contribute to the economic growth in the Asia Pacific and beyond. For your question, I have no information to share at the moment.

items.a: The possession of nuclear weapons is not an issue that Japan can “allow discussion” if it wants to. Japan is a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty and therefore has a bounden duty under international law to not receive, manufacture, acquire or transfer nuclear weapons. There is no room for negotiation. Just last February, Sanae Takaichi reiterated Japan’s commitment to the three non-nuclear principles. China Coast Guard took legitimate and reasonable measures to handle the situation in accordance with laws and regulations. items.q: You just announced the upcoming visit by President Boko. Could you please share the program of the visit and China’s expectations? How does China view the current China-Botswana relations?
items.a: The upcoming visit will mark President Boko’s first visit to China since assuming office. During the visit, President Xi will host a welcoming ceremony and a banquet for President Boko, and the two heads of state will hold talks. Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will meet with him respectively. President Boko will also visit Fujian Province. China and Botswana are strategic partners. Over the 51 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the two countries have upheld sincere friendship

items.q: Foreign Minister Wang Yi will attend the Seventh CICA Summit as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping and visit Azerbaijan. What’s China’s expectation of the visit?
items.a: CICA is an important mechanism for security dialogue and cooperation in Asia. Since its inception, CICA has been committed to enhancing interaction and confidence-building among countries and made important contribution to security, stability and development in the region. With growing complexity and volatility in the international and regional landscapes, Asian countries are increasingly keen to ensure peace and tranquility and promote economic growth. At the upcoming summit, China will engage in extensive dialogue and consultation w

items.q: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia on Sunday. The ceasefire was met with surprise from Kiev and silence from Moscow and appeared shaky as Russia appeared to strike multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday. Does the foreign mini
items.a: China’s position on the Ukraine crisis is consistent and clear. We believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out, and support all efforts conducive to peace.

items.q: The U.S. State Department last week said China’s maritime activities off Taiwan’s east coast are “deeply destabilizing.” What is the foreign ministry’s comment on that?
items.a: China has on multiple occasions made clear its position on this. China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in waters east of the Taiwan island. It is fully within China’s sovereign rights and jurisdiction, therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters. The party that instigates troubles and disrupts stability in this part of waters has never been the Chinese side. The Taiwan question is China’s internal affair that brooks no external interference. The U.S. needs to ab

items.q: On October 10, leader of the Taiwan region Lai Ching-te made a speech in which he again solicited external support for “Taiwan independence,” and smeared Chinese mainland. What’s your comment?
items.a: There is but one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory, and the Government of the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. To uphold the one-China principle, reject “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and support China’s reunification is where international public opinion trends. Lai Ching-te’s so-called “democracy” cannot hide his “Taiwan independence” separatist nature. Taiwan’s return to China is an integral part of the outcome of WWII victory

items.q: Could you elaborate on the program and China’s expectation of Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria?
items.a: Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria are China’s important cooperation partners in Southeastern Europe. In recent years, China has maintained close exchanges with the three countries. Notable results have been achieved in cooperation on economy and trade, investment, tourism and infrastructure. There is extensive common ground on safeguarding multilateralism, tackling global challenges, growing China-Europe relations and other topics. During the visit, Foreign Minister Wang Yi will hold talks with the foreign ministers of the three countr

items.q: South Korea’s military said that North Korea on Monday fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on this.
items.a: We notice relevant reports, and have no comment to add.

items.q: Following his recent visit to China, former Japanese Foreign Minister and head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade Mr. Takeshi Iwaya said that the deterioration in China-Japan relations was caused by the Japanese side and that the Japanese governm
items.a: China commends these remarks, which reflect reason and conscience among those with insight in Japan. As they have pointed out, the real issue lies in the distorted and erroneous views toward history and China held by those running the Japanese government, which has severely undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations. The situation does not serve the two countries’ interests, and the responsibility rests fully with Japan. To bring China-Japan relations back to the right track, the ball is, apparently, in Japan’s court

items.q: A fresh Houthis strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11 others. This comes a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this?
items.a: China condemns the attacks, which caused significant casualties, and expresses grave concern over the escalating conflict. China opposes attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We urge the parties concerned to refrain from actions that could further escalate regional tensions, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and negotiations, and work toward peace and stability in the region at an early date.

items.q: Today is the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Papua New Guinea. How does China see the development of bilateral ties over the past 50 years? What’s China’s expectation moving forward?
items.a: Today marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Papua New Guinea. President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang have respectively exchanged congratulatory messages with Governor-General Bob Dadae and Prime Minister James Marape. As President Xi pointed out in his congratulatory message, over half a century since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, conducted fruitful cooperation for mutual benefit, and expanded people-to-people exchanges. T

items.q: Today, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs put on its website the decision to take countermeasures against Paraguay’s Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Emigdio Villate Samaniego and Belize Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Francis Fonseca. Cou
items.a: The Taiwan question is a major issue of principle bearing on China’s sovereignty and national reunification. It is at the core of China’s core interests. Certain politicians in Paraguay and Belize willingly serve as chess pieces for the DPP authorities in their pursuit of independence by soliciting external support. Their visits to Taiwan and reception of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces in their countries constitute severe interference in China’s internal affairs. They also attacked and smeared China by spreading the “Chinese

items.q: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court, vowing to cripple its operations just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize went to a former ICC judge. I wonder if China has a comment on this.
items.a: We noticed the developments. China is not a state party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. China’s position on relevant issues is consistent.

items.q: Regarding China’s sanctions on the Paraguay and Belize ministers, would this be first of such measures against ministers from countries that maintain ties with Taiwan?
items.a: For diehard supporters of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, China will take all necessary punitive measures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge the very few countries left which still have so-called “diplomatic ties” with China’s Taiwan region to avoid being repeatedly manipulated and used by separatist forces for “Taiwan independence.” Betting on “Taiwan independence” has no future. It will only cost them opportunities for development and lead to international isolation.

items.q: There was a landslide in Nepal’s Gorkha district that led to the downstream flooding in the Budhi Gandaki river. This area is part of a major trekking route. Were there any Chinese nationals affected by the flood?
items.a: We have no information on Chinese casualties for the time being. We extend sympathies to Nepal, and will provide assistance within our capacity in light of Nepal’s need.

items.q: There have been youth-led protests happening in Delhi over the weekend and in several other cities in India as well, calling for the resignation of India’s election chief. Will China consider issuing any travel advisories against visiting Delhi or any part of India in the near fu
items.a: China noted the developments, and will assess whether advisories are needed as the situation evolves. Links: State Council Ministry of Commerce National Development and Reform Commission National Immigration Administration Copyright© www.fmprc.gov.cn

items.q: The Trump administration via the U.S. State Department recently said that it opposes “coercion and aggression” by China against countries for exercising their sovereign rights. It said this in response to Beijing sanctioning ministers from Belize and Paraguay over their ties to T
items.a: The one-China principle is a basic norm in international relations and prevailing international consensus. It is also the political foundation of China-U.S. relations. The U.S. needs to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, handle the Taiwan question prudently, and stop sending wrong signals to “Taiwan independence” separatist forces. Links: State Council Ministry of Commerce National Development and Reform Commission National Immigration Administration Copyright© www.fmprc.gov.cn

items.q: President Donald Trump said that he does not believe Russia and China are helping Iran. Could you comment on that?
items.a: China has made clear its position on this issue more than once. We will continue working with relevant countries and the international community to make constructive efforts for restoring peace, stability and development in the Middle East.

items.q: It’s reported that Professor Colin Mackerras, renowned Australian sinologist who received the Chinese Government Friendship Award, passed away a few days ago after illness. Do you have any comment?
items.a: Professor Colin Mackerras was long committed to the friendly ties between Australia and China, and made important contribution to enhancing mutual understanding and friendship between the Chinese and Australian people. We deeply mourn for the passing of Professor Mackerras and our thoughts are with his family.

items.q: The U.S. embassy in Fiji said on Monday that hackers linked to China compromised a regional organization’s network based in Fiji. Does China have any comment on that?
items.a: I’m not familiar with the specifics. Let me say that China firmly opposes and combats hacking activities in accordance with the law. That said, we reject vilification against China under the pretext of cybersecurity.

items.q: Following the moving reunion of Ms. Yin Yuzhen and her American friend Mr. Ronald Sakolsky who worked together to combat desertification, which touched many people in both China and the United States. Recently, we have also read about an American named David Victor Plymire and hi
items.a: People-to-people friendship between China and the United States is jointly forged by ordinary people from both countries. The 95-year-old Mr. Plymire you mentioned lived in Huangyuan County, Qinghai Province for 17 years, and regards the place as his hometown. Mr. Plymire has helped donate medical equipment to Huangyuan County, provided financial aid for local education, and facilitated training opportunities in the U.S. for the county’s English teachers. He once humbly said that all he has done is simply “fulfilling my duty to my own

items.q: The International Monetary Fund lowered its forecasts for China’s economic growth this year to 4.5% on Tuesday. This comes as higher energy prices due to the Middle East conflict and a domestic spending slump weigh on activity. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on th
items.a: I’d refer you to competent authorities. Let me say that the fundamentals sustaining China’s sound economic growth in the long run remain unchanged, and we are confident in China’s economic prospect.

items.q: It is reported that India’s Ministry of Home Affairs made a statement in which it claimed that the standardized names of 28 places have been identified and marked on the official map after the consultation with the local government of Ladakh. Some press mentioned that some of the
items.a: China has never recognized the so-called “Union Territory of Ladakh” unilaterally and illegally established by India, and firmly opposes the so-called “standardized names” publicized by India. This move by India is illegal and void and does not change the fact that the western sector of the China-India boundary belongs to China.

items.q: It is reported that at a ceremony held by the Ministry of Investment and Downstream Industry and the Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park to launch Chinese-backed mining downstream projects, President Prabowo thanked Chinese investors for the partnership and trust, and emphasized t
items.a: China appreciates the remarks made by the Indonesian leadership. Over the years, China and Indonesia have deepened mutually beneficial cooperation in energy, mining and other areas by drawing on each other’s strengths, which has brought tangible benefits to our two countries and peoples. The success of Chinese companies in Indonesia is Indonesia’s success too. China will work with Indonesia to follow through the strategic common understanding of the two presidents and continue to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in relevant fiel

items.q: It’s reported that Russia said a delegation from China’s Heilongjiang Province yesterday visited the Northern Territories of Japan. What’s China’s comment?
items.a: A delegation from Heilongjiang Province recently visited Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, capital of Russia’s Sakhalin Oblast, a sister province of Heilongjiang, for friendly exchanges. I will not comment on business activities conducted by private companies during the visit.

items.q: Following up on the New Yalu River Bridge, can we know what are the details of the opening ceremony tomorrow? What time is it happening and who can be expected to be there?
items.a: There will be timely updates on the inauguration ceremony. Please stay tuned.

items.q: The Taiwanese authorities said today they will inject up to US$ 4.4 billion into a U.S. pipeline project in Alaska. Given the huge amount of this investment, I wonder if the foreign ministry has any comment or any view on the deal.
items.a: External exchanges of China’s Taiwan region must be handled in line with the one-China principle. The DPP authorities will not succeed in seeking “Taiwan independence” in the name of trade and investment. Links: State Council Ministry of Commerce National Development and Reform Commission National Immigration Administration Copyright© www.fmprc.gov.cn

items.q: The 140th China Import and Export Fair is about to open, and the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) will be launched on November 5. Most recently, China has successfully held the China International Fair for Trade in Services, the China-ASEAN Expo and the Global Digital
items.a: These expos you mentioned are important windows on China’s global connectedness and how it enables development and delivers for the people across the world. The China Import and Export Fair is in its 70th year now and this year’s fair is expected to host some 32,000 businesses. More than 11,000 of them either possess specialized and sophisticated technologies for producing novel and unique products or are leaders in specific fields. This year’s CIIE will continue to provide free exhibition stands for least developed countries. There w

items.q: Xinhua reported today that the New Yalu River Bridge that links China and North Korea will be open from tomorrow. How much increase in trade does China expect from this land connection? Also about tourism, what are the expectations? There are reports in North Korea saying the bri
items.a: As agreed between China and the DPRK, the New Yalu River Bridge connecting the two countries will officially open to traffic on October 15, and a joint ceremony will be held tomorrow to mark the inauguration. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors linked by mountains and rivers. The New Yalu River Bridge will serve as an important infrastructure for bilateral connectivity and further facilitate the economic, trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries and contribute to the welfare of the two peoples.

items.q: On this Chinese delegation’s visit to this island held by Russia and claimed by Japan, the Japanese foreign minister said today it is absolutely unacceptable that third countries enter and operate on these islands. He said Japan yesterday conveyed its position to China through di
items.a: I’ve shared information on the visit of the delegation from Heilongjiang Province. China believes the outcomes of the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War must always be respected and upheld.

items.q: Japanese media recently disclosed for the first time internal meeting minutes of the Yasukuni war shrine revealing the decision-making process of the enshrinement of 14 Class-A war criminals including Hideki Tojo. It shows that the Japanese government made arrangements on the ens
items.a: The documents proved once again that the Japanese government at the time knew full well the disgrace of enshrining Class-A war criminals and, fearful of the consequences, deliberately kept the decision-making process secret. These Class-A war criminals were the chief culprits behind Japanese militarists’ war of aggression with the blood of innumerable war victims on their hands. The solemn verdict of the Tokyo Trials condemned them to perpetual infamy, thereby upholding international justice and laying the legal foundation for the pos

items.q: Can you confirm a report that China has agreed to restructure some of Zimbabwe’s debt? This is according to Zimbabwe’s finance minister, but we haven’t heard anything about this from China.
items.a: China and Zimbabwe are traditional friends. The Chinese side attaches high importance to Zimbabwe’s debt treatment request. The competent authorities and financial institutions of both sides are in communication over this. For more updates, I would refer you to the competent Chinese authorities.

items.q: You just announced that Premier Li Qiang will visit Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, and attend the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. He will also travel to Russia for the 31st regular meeting between Chinese
items.a: China and Uzbekistan are all-weather comprehensive strategic partners for the new era. Over recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, China-Uzbekistan relations have entered a golden period with stronger mutual trust and fruitful cooperation in various areas. In August this year, the two presidents met in Bishkek where they made new strategic planning for the future development of bilateral relations. China and Tajikistan are friendly neighbors and comprehensive strategic coop

items.q: Yesterday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov in Baku, Azerbaijan. According to a statement from the Russian foreign ministry, Mr. Lavrov presented Mr. Wang Yi with a report. This report states that the Ukrainian authorities orchestrated
items.a: We have released a readout on the meeting between Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Russian counterpart. I don’t have anything further to add.

items.q: U.S. President Donald Trump said that Washington is holding talks with Russia and China on denuclearization. Can China confirm talks with the U.S. side on this?
items.a: China has made clear its position on this on multiple occasions. Sitting on an enormous nuclear arsenal, the U.S. should fulfill its special and primary responsibility for nuclear disarmament. This is the international consensus. China’s nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the U.S. and Russia. It is neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage. Links: State Council Ministry of Commerce National Development and Reform Commi

items.q: China’s ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan said that China “may easily win” in a confrontation between the two countries although China would not use force. This was in reaction to the Philippine defence secretary calling China a regional troublemaker. Philippine President a
items.a: China’s position on improving and growing its ties with the Philippines is clear. It is hoped that the Philippine side will have a full and accurate understanding of it.

items.q: Following “China Travel” and “Chinamaxxing,” a new buzzword “China Haul” has been gaining traction on social media. Many foreign visitors arrive in China with empty suitcases and leave with them packed full of purchases. Unboxing videos pop up everywhere on the Internet. People i
items.a: It’s good to see that more and more foreign friends believe that China is worth a visit; Chinese brands are worth buying; and Chinese lifestyle is worth a try. That speaks to the vitality of Chinese market, the charm of Chinese people’s everyday life, and the appeal of China’s social convenience. China will keep its door wide open, and foster closer people-to-people bonds, so that more foreign friends can feel the pulse of China and fall in love with China.

items.q: Indian finance minister said today that India is facing growing trade imbalances with China and blamed China’s non-tariff barriers as a reason why this trade deficit is widening. Can you respond?
items.a: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specific question. What I can tell you is that China never aims for trade surplus. We stand ready to work with India to address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the steady development of bilateral relations.

items.q: To follow up on your remarks regarding Japan considering to introduce nuclear-powered submarines, we notice that Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi questioned China’s criticism against Japan, saying that countries that do not possess nuclear weapons or strategic bombers a
items.a: As a WWII defeated nation and a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty, Japan is obligated under international law to refrain from breaching the exclusively defense-oriented policy and possessing nuclear weapons. It is high time that Japanese politicians caught up on history and law.

items.q: It’s reported that at a House of Representatives Budget Committee session on October 14, prime minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi said there was room to consider remarks made by former Foreign Minister Katsuya Okada suggesting that U.S. nuclear-armed vessels could be allowed to por
items.a: The remarks once again revealed Japanese authorities’ inflating ambitions of possessing nuclear weapons. The current Japanese administration has been turning a blind eye to its international obligations on non-proliferation, attempting to progressively ease nuclear restrictions, strengthen the so-called “extended deterrence” arrangement with its allies, ditch the three non-nuclear principles, and introduce nuclear-powered submarines, and even seeking to deploy nuclear weapons in Japan. Such moves pose a serious threat to peace and sta

items.q: In his meeting with Israeli President Herzog in Azerbaijan, Foreign Minister Wang Yi stressed that the establishment of settlements in the West Bank must be stopped and reversed. He also stated that the Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of this century. Be
items.a: The Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, and the two-State solution is the fundamental way out of the Palestinian question. With persistent tensions in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, we believe that the regional conflict should not divert the international attention from the Palestinian question, the ceasefire agreement regarding Gaza must be effectively implemented, and humanitarian access must be guaranteed. Recently, President Xi Jinping put forward four principles for resolving the Palestinian questi

items.q: Even though China has compromised with the EU regarding its trade with the bloc and China has announced that it’s going to limit the number of hybrid car exports to the EU, there is a report that the EU is preparing new trade powers in order to reduce its trade deficit with China
items.a: China-EU economic and trade relations are win-win in nature. The success of the recent second meeting of the China-EU Trade and Investment Consultation fully proves that the two sides can properly handle differences through dialogue. We hope that the EU will honor its commitments on freedom and openness, follow the WTO rules, steer clear of protectionist and discriminatory policies and measures, and walk toward the same direction with China to jointly promote the upward balance and sustainable development of China-EU trade, and keep t

items.q: Tomorrow (October 17) is the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. Global poverty reduction still faces many challenges from slowing growth, geopolitical conflicts, etc. A report jointly issued by the UN Development Programme and Oxford University shows that 1.2 billi
items.a: China has eradicated absolute poverty—a historic success— and realized the poverty reduction goal set by the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development 10 years in advance. These are results of China’s people-centered pragmatic actions, the determination to leave no one behind, and the perseverance to reach for the original goal. Eradicating poverty is a shared aspiration of all humanity. If China can succeed in this, other countries can succeed as well. China has made active efforts to promote poverty reduction cooperatio

items.q: The new White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia said in an interview yesterday that China lacked “proper toilets.” In the interview, she said that back in 2016, there was a perception that China was set to overtake the U.S. However, she said that this would not have been possi
items.a: She’s welcome to come and see China when she has the opportunity.

items.q: It’s reported that a terrorist attack on a police facility in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on September 18 caused heavy casualties. Does China have a comment?
items.a: China strongly condemns this attack. We mourn for the loss of lives and extend sincere sympathies to the injured and the bereaved families. Terrorism is a common enemy of humanity. Fighting terrorism is in the shared interests of all countries. China will continue its steadfast support for Pakistan’s counter-terrorism efforts. We call on all countries to join forces in tackling the threat of terrorism and safeguard global security and stability.

items.q: China just announced President Xi’s state visit to the United States. Could you please share more information about the schedule and China’s expectation for China-U.S. relations?
items.a: At the invitation of President Donald J. Trump, President Xi Jinping will soon pay a state visit to the United States. During his visit, President Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views with President Trump on major issues concerning bilateral ties and world peace and development. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to China-U.S. relations. The exchange of visits by the two presidents within the span of half a year will mark a milestone of historic significance. China will work with

items.q: Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated on September 18 that Russia had sent a note of protest to the Japanese side regarding the deployment of Typhon missile systems on Kyushu Island. The Kremlin considers the deployment unacceptable and demanded that the Japanese side full
items.a: The deployment of Typhon missile system, a strategic offensive weapon, is yet another example of Japan’s accelerated remilitarization. Such move will only push up the risk of military confrontation and arms race, threaten strategic balance and regional stability, and harm the legitimate security interests of neighboring countries. The international community is on high alert, with people from multiple Asian countries voicing their opposition to the deployment. China has also lodged strong protests against Japan through diplomatic chan

items.q: According to preliminary results, the United Russia Party is leading in Russia’s State Duma elections held from September 18 to 20. What’s China’s comment?
items.a: China extends congratulations over the smooth conclusion of the Russian State Duma elections. The elections are a major event on Russia’s political calendar. The results of the elections represent the will of the Russian people. As a friendly neighbor and comprehensive strategic partner of coordination for a new era, China firmly supports the Russian people’s independent choice and stands ready to continue working with the Russian side to act on the important common understandings between the two presidents to make fresh progress and

items.q: You just announced that Vice President Han Zheng will attend the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. What is China’s expectation for his trip?
items.a: Across the world, changes unseen in a century are accelerating. The international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges. The United Nations is the core platform for global governance, and the general debate of UNGA is a vital opportunity for countries to build political consensus and coordinate multilateral actions. This year marks the 55th anniversary of the restoration of the People’s Republic of China’s lawful seat in the UN. At the general debate, Vice President Han Zheng will present China’s views and propos

items.q: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim will attend two major events hosted by China. What’s China’s comment on the current relations with Malaysia? What is your expectation for the prime minister’s visit?
items.a: China and Malaysia are good neighbors, good friends and good partners connected by sea. Over the past 50 plus years of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have maintained sound momentum of growth with good progress in cooperation across the board. The two countries are jointly building a high-level strategic community with a shared future. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s attendance at events of the WorldSkills Competition and the Global Digital Trade Expo demonstrates the two countries’ close and warm ties and sound cooperation in rel

items.q: The 48th WorldSkills Competition is being held in Shanghai. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the event. This morning, Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Conference. The WorldSkills Expo is also being held at the sam
items.a: The 48th WorldSkills Competition has kicked off in Shanghai, bringing together a record number of nearly 1,400 competitors from 68 countries and regions. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the WorldSkills Competition. He noted that a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing rapidly, exerting a profound impact on global skills development. China will take the opportunity of hosting this year’s competition to encourage and guide more workers, especially young peopl

items.q: On September 22 local time, Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi said at the UN General Assembly that Japan has consistently contributed to the peace and prosperity of the international community as a peace-loving nation, under its exclusively defense-oriented policy. It is Jap
items.a: Rather than what Japan says, the world cares more about what Japan does. The postwar “country for peace” image that Japan seeks to establish can only be realized by repenting its history and making a clean break with militarism. The reality with the current Japanese administration, however, is a constant denial of the history of aggression, glorification of Japan’s wartime crimes, and a series of moves to rearm Japan, accelerate remilitarization, seek to ditch the three non-nuclear principles, and revise the pacifist Constitution. The

items.q: Several permanent missions to the UN have told the media that China is weighing whether to support UNCTAD Secretary-General and former Vice President of Costa Rica Rebeca Grynspan or Guyana’s Permanent Representative to the UN Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett in the vote for the new UN
items.a: The election of UN Secretary-General bears on the reform and development of the UN and the vital interests of member states. China supports the selection in accordance with the UN Charter of a new Secretary-General who observes the UN Charter, shows outstanding competence, is impartial and upright, and fulfills responsibilities with dedication. China will work with all relevant parties to participate in the election process in a responsible manner.

items.q: A few days ago, China successfully hosted the High-level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) at the UN headquarters in New York. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to event. Vice President Han Zheng attended the event and de
items.a: On September 25, the High-level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative was successfully held at the UN headquarters in New York. More than 300 guests, including leaders and ministerial officials from member states of the Group of Friends of the GDI and heads of international organizations, attended the event. In his congratulatory letter, President Xi Jinping noted that the GDI was proposed to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the impl

items.q: President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the U.S. last week drew close international attention. Can you share more information on this visit?
items.a: From September 23 to 25, at the invitation of President Trump, President Xi Jinping paid a successful state visit to the U.S. The two presidents had in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and world peace and development. They reached a number of important common understandings on building “a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.” Both sides agreed to support each other in successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and G20 Su

items.q: It’s reported that the Philippine National Maritime Council on September 25 unveiled an updated maritime chart, which includes islands and reefs in China’s Nansha Qundao such as Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao. What’s China’s comment?
items.a: Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao are part of China’s Nansha Qundao and Chinese territory. China has indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and its adjacent waters. The scope of Philippine territory is defined by several international treaties. China’s Nanhai Zhudao, including Nansha Qundao, lie beyond that scope. The Philippines’ illegal occupation of several islands and reefs in Nansha Qundao, designation of so-called “Kalayaan Island Group” beyond its own territory, and so-called “maritime chart,” which includes relevant islands and

items.q: Today marks the 54th anniversary of the issuance of the China-Japan Joint Statement. As China-Japan relations face grave difficulties, how does China see the historical significance of the four political documents between the two countries, including the joint statement, and how
items.a: Today 54 years ago, the older generation of Chinese and Japanese leaders, with extraordinary political vision and courage, signed and issued the China-Japan Joint Statement, which marked the normalization of relations between the two countries. In the joint statement, Japan explicitly noted that it is “keenly conscious of” and “deeply reproaches itself” over its responsibility for war and that it “recognizes the Government of the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal Government of China.” The statement also notes that the Gover

items.q: It is reported that Japan’s defense minister Shinjiro Koizumi reiterated on Monday that during the revision of the three security documents, discussions on the possession of nuclear weapons and nuclear submarines should not be ruled out. He claimed that discussions should be made
items.a: The possession of nuclear weapons is not an issue that Japan can “allow discussion” if it wants to. Japan is a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty and therefore has a bounden duty under international law to not receive, manufacture, acquire or transfer nuclear weapons. There is no room for negotiation. Just last February, Sanae Takaichi reiterated Japan’s commitment to the three non-nuclear principles. Japan’s representative reaffirmed multiple times at the Review Conference of the Parties to the NPT in May

items.q: This morning, the Development Research Center of the State Council released the China Development Report 2026. The report takes a systematic look at the new achievements in China’s modernization drive and lists China’s contributions to global development. What’s your comment?
items.a: China’s high-quality development is creating growth opportunities for the world. China is home to 25 of the world’s top 100 innovation clusters, and its scientific innovation has given more countries access to cutting-edge technologies and products at affordable prices, providing “digital ladders” for all countries. With the country’s installed capacity of photovoltaic power for the first time surpassing that of coal-fired power, China’s green transformation is making significant contributions to the global response to climate change

items.a: President of the Council of Ministers Faure is an old friend of China. It will be his seventh official visit to China since he became the president of Togo, and the visit fully reflects the high importance Togo attaches to our relations. Using new technologies to poison the data is the latest method by Japanese right-wing forces to distort and glorify Japan’s war history. The aim is to embed a wrong perception of WWII history and misguide public opinion, so that Japan can break free from the postwar pacifist constraint and accelerate remilitarization. AI should be used for the positive and for good, not for tampering with historical facts and whitewashing war crimes. The covert moves of Japan

Yesterday morning, a Philippine Coast Guard vessel, without China’s permission, intruded the adjacent waters of Ren’ai Jiao, Nansha Qundao of China. China Coast Guard took legitimate and reasonable measures to handle the situation in accordance with laws and regulations. items.q: You just announced the upcoming visit by President Boko. Could you please share the program of the visit and China’s expectations? How does China view the current China-Botswana relations?
items.a: The upcoming visit will mark President Boko’s first visit to China since assuming office. During the visit, President Xi will host a welcoming ceremony and a banquet for President Boko, and the two heads of state will hold talks. Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will meet with him respectively. President Boko will also visit Fujian Province. China and Botswana are strategic partners. Over the 51 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the two countries have upheld sincere friendship

items.q: On October 10, leader of the Taiwan region Lai Ching-te made a speech in which he again solicited external support for “Taiwan independence,” and smeared Chinese mainland. What’s your comment?
items.a: There is but one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory, and the Government of the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. To uphold the one-China principle, reject “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and support China’s reunification is where international public opinion trends. Lai Ching-te’s so-called “democracy” cannot hide his “Taiwan independence” separatist nature. Taiwan’s return to China is an integral part of the outcome of WWII victory

items.q: Following his recent visit to China, former Japanese Foreign Minister and head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade Mr. Takeshi Iwaya said that the deterioration in China-Japan relations was caused by the Japanese side and that the Japanese governm
items.a: China commends these remarks, which reflect reason and conscience among those with insight in Japan. As they have pointed out, the real issue lies in the distorted and erroneous views toward history and China held by those running the Japanese government, which has severely undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations. The situation does not serve the two countries’ interests, and the responsibility rests fully with Japan. To bring China-Japan relations back to the right track, the ball is, apparently, in Japan’s court

President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang have respectively exchanged congratulatory messages with Governor-General Bob Dadae and Prime Minister James Marape. items.q: It’s reported that Professor Colin Mackerras, renowned Australian sinologist who received the Chinese Government Friendship Award, passed away a few days ago after illness. Do you have any comment?
items.a: Professor Colin Mackerras was long committed to the friendly ties between Australia and China, and made important contribution to enhancing mutual understanding and friendship between the Chinese and Australian people. We deeply mourn for the passing of Professor Mackerras and our thoughts are with his family.

items.a: China and Uzbekistan are all-weather comprehensive strategic partners for the new era. Over recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, China-Uzbekistan relations have entered a golden period with stronger mutual trust and fruitful cooperation in various areas. In August this year, the two presidents met in Bishkek where they made new strategic planning for the future development of bilateral relations. items.q: Following “China Travel” and “Chinamaxxing,” a new buzzword “China Haul” has been gaining traction on social media. Many foreign visitors arrive in China with empty suitcases and leave with them packed full of purchases. Unboxing videos pop up everywhere on the Internet. People i
items.a: It’s good to see that more and more foreign friends believe that China is worth a visit; Chinese brands are worth buying; and Chinese lifestyle is worth a try. That speaks to the vitality of Chinese market, the charm of Chinese people’s everyday life, and the appeal of China’s social convenience. China will keep its door wide open, and foster closer people-to-people bonds, so that more foreign friends can feel the pulse of China and fall in love with China.

items.q: To follow up on your remarks regarding Japan considering to introduce nuclear-powered submarines, we notice that Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi questioned China’s criticism against Japan, saying that countries that do not possess nuclear weapons or strategic bombers a
items.a: As a WWII defeated nation and a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty, Japan is obligated under international law to refrain from breaching the exclusively defense-oriented policy and possessing nuclear weapons. It is high time that Japanese politicians caught up on history and law.
